$doc: The securaCV hub provisioning bundle: the self-contained payload (plan + curated Frigate config + executor + runner) that provisions a freshly-flashed hub with one command. Generated so the bundle can never carry stale code — each file's SHA-256 is pinned, and CI regenerates this manifest and fails on drift.

first_boot.what_works_today: From the Advanced SSH & Web Terminal add-on (python3 + SUPERVISOR_TOKEN present): copy this bundle and run `sh provision.sh` — `--dry-run` first to preview.
candidate_hooks: A curated HA package/automation seeded into CONFIG/ that shells out to the runner on first HA start (HA Core can reach http://supervisor with its own token).
A first-boot provisioner add-on the flasher pre-registers, which runs the bundle.
first_boot.note: HAOS ignores boot-partition files it doesn't recognise, so a bundle that isn't auto-run is harmless — worst case is a normal onboarding, never a broken boot. The write side is hub_io::seed (the CONFIG/ tree, already used for Wi-Fi); which hook actually auto-runs the bundle is what on-hardware validation pins.
